deployment.sessionNewNote: Showing the newly sent blocks in each recorded request received by the Latet server.

deployment.requestNotSentText: This request was not forwarded on the protected provider path. The recorded text is kept encrypted in this identity's server history for the configured retention time; this view displays it in your browser.

deployment.projectNoFile: No repository file is available to this server view.
deployment.projectRepoReadOnly: These repository settings were supplied by the connected agent. This server view cannot read, create or change files on that computer.
deployment.stoppedHelp: Latet stopped this protected request before forwarding this value in clear to the model provider. Click it to inspect it or mark it Not sensitive.
deployment.stopped: Stopped before this value was forwarded in clear on the protected model/provider path.
deployment.statsBlockedHelp: Protected requests stopped before forwarding to the model provider
deployment.profileBalanced: Secrets, your own terms, personal data (emails, phones, IBANs, codice fiscale, partita IVA, cards) and identity supplied to this server space. The default for code work.
deployment.nerDescription: When its model is available, name detection on the Latet server can find names of people and street addresses that patterns cannot identify.
deployment.nerToggleHelp: Uses the server's name-detection model when available. Administrators install and maintain it.
deployment.reviewerDescription: The administrator-configured reviewer service can read original text left in clear by the detectors before forwarding to the model provider. It can add masking, never remove it.
deployment.ocrOn: Text recognition runs on the Latet server when available, covering detected values with surrogates.
deployment.reviewBlock: Keep these details from the reviewer (default)
deployment.reviewBlockHelp: Latet stops these auto-mode review requests before forwarding them to the reviewer. Claude Code treats its reviewer as unavailable, refuses those actions and does not ask you. Data already received by Latet is not erased.
deployment.imagesHelp: Images are processed on the Latet server; administrators provide text recognition. Send does not override an enabled server check that refuses unread images. Only masked requires readable, masked images and excludes PDFs. Don't send excludes images and PDFs. Other server checks still apply.
deployment.destinationsHelp: Destinations reported by connected agents or configured on the server. Registration is not an audit of installed agents or their current settings.
deployment.destinationsEmpty: No additional destinations are reported here. This does not confirm how every connected agent is routed.
deployment.integrationsCli: On each connected computer, these commands check its connection and configure its agents to use Latet.
deployment.pending: Deployment information could not be loaded. Retry the connection to load it.
deployment.ocrUnavailable: Text recognition is unavailable on the Latet server. Ask the server's administrators to check its runtime and model.
deployment.nerUnavailable: Name detection is unavailable on the Latet server. Ask the server's administrators to check its runtime and model.
deployment.historyClear: Every recorded exchange in this identity's server history is deleted. The vault is kept, so masking and restoring go on as before. This can't be undone.
deployment.identityHelp: Identity supplied by connected computers: user names in paths, host names, and git names and emails.
deployment.reviewerHelp: Found by the administrator-configured reviewer, which can read original text the detectors left in clear. A dashed line marks a judgement, not a pattern match.
deployment.nerHelp: Found by the name-detection model on the Latet server: names, street addresses and cities. A dashed line marks a judgement, not a pattern match.
deployment.blockedHelp: Latet stopped this protected request before forwarding it to the model provider. This does not describe other network traffic.
deployment.imageHelp: An image was read on the Latet server ({{detail}}). Masked: detected values were covered with surrogates. Withheld: it could not be read and was excluded from the model request.
deployment.outboundHelp: A provider or external tool got, or would have got, a surrogate. It acts on the surrogate, not the original. This does not inspect arbitrary tool traffic.
deployment.uninspectedHelp: Part of this request was not inspected ({{detail}}). The flag alone does not prove it was forwarded. An enabled server check refuses unread images; a rewritten request may withhold them. Protection-off calls follow their own policy.
deployment.pluginHelp: The supported Claude Code plugin flow stopped this model request. Text may already have reached Latet through its helper or bridge; this does not mean there was no network traffic.
deployment.reviewHappened: Claude Code asked its auto-mode reviewer about an action. The request carried {{details}} reported by the connected agent, which your rules keep from that reviewer, so it was not forwarded to it.
deployment.notForwarded: This protected request was not forwarded to the model provider. This does not describe other network traffic or erase data already received by Latet.
deployment.toolInputMeant: This protected request was not forwarded to the model provider. This does not describe other network traffic or erase data already received by Latet. Claude Code sends a tool's schema with every request once it has loaded the tool, and every tool's schema after an error: its requests stop here until you change something.
deployment.imagesTodo: Remove the unread attachment or ask the server's administrators to check text recognition. Your image policy cannot make an enabled server check forward an image it could not read.
deployment.doctorTodo: Run latet doctor on the connected computer to check its connection. Ask the server's administrators to investigate a server failure.
deployment.imagesHappened: Your image policy requires readable, masked images. Latet could not read {{what}}: availability, capacity, time limits or the input format may prevent it.
deployment.reviewerHappened: Your rules require the configured reviewer to check new text. Its service could not complete a trusted check, or asked to stop this request.
deployment.reviewerTodo: Ask the server's administrators to check the reviewer service. Your own reviewer policy remains in Rules; its endpoint, model, certificate and key are set by the administrators.
deployment.outboundHappened: The model asked {{tools}} to use {{types}} that Latet had replaced. This provider or external tool would have acted on the surrogate: searched for someone else, opened the wrong page or used an invented address.
deployment.outboundTodo: Only if the original may be sent to this provider or external tool, mark it Not sensitive and ask the model to try again. Otherwise keep it masked.
deployment.outboundRanMeant: What the tool found or did concerns the surrogate, not the original; its answer may attribute it to the real value. This call used the surrogate, which is not a claim about other network traffic.
deployment.vault: This identity's originals and surrogates are kept sealed on the Latet server. Authorized dashboard views can deliver originals to this browser. Clearing history keeps the vault.
deployment.integrations: Registered destinations and connection checks for this server space. The server does not scan installed agents on connected computers.
deployment.reviewerEnabled: Administrators configure this reviewer service. When selected, it can read original text the detectors left in clear.

errors.settingsWaitingForOthers: It lowers protection, so it waits for whoever decides on it (Approvals). The settings in use stay as they are.
errors.repositoriesUnchecked: Latet could not read every repository it has seen just now (one may be on a share that does not answer, or in a file it may not read), so nothing changed. Try again once they can be read.

errors.repoFileUnavailable: This project's latet.yaml cannot be read just now, so nothing was saved over it. Try again in a moment.
errors.settingsSavedChangePending: Your settings were saved, but the pending change could not be refreshed. Refresh the dashboard before making another change.
errors.companySignIn: This change applies to everyone on this server, so it needs a session opened with your company account. Sign out, sign in with your company account, then make the change again.
errors.settingsTooManyProjects: These settings name more projects than the server keeps for one person, so nothing was saved. Remove your settings for some projects, then save again.
errors.settingsDropsShared: This would remove {{items}} set for everyone on this server, so nothing was saved. Only the server's administrators can remove them.
errors.destinationRefused: {{url}}: a destination of your own on this server needs an address that can be used, reached over https, and leading neither to the server itself nor inside its network. A destination reached in clear or inside the network can be set for everyone by its administrators.
errors.reviewerKeyServer: {{setting}}: on a server no setting says where the local reviewer's key is read from. The server gives it, as its administrators set it.
errors.repoInClear: {{setting}}: a repository file cannot hold this, as it would leave values in clear there (a recognizer that lets what it finds through, or a recognizer, a term or a field rule of a type let through). Put it in your own settings for the project, where a change that lowers protection waits for approval.

rewrite.label: Rewrite
rewrite.help: Gateway mode. Latet replaced sensitive values with surrogates before forwarding, and put the originals back into the answer.

verify.label: Verify
verify.help: Client mode, used for Claude Code. The plugin masked values inside Claude Code; Latet checked the request, then forwarded it unchanged or blocked it.

passthrough.label: Passthrough
passthrough.help: Not inspected. Latet doesn't understand this route or body, so it was forwarded as it was.

SECRET.label: Secret
SECRET.help: Credentials: API keys, tokens, passwords, private keys, connection strings.

PII.label: Personal data
PII.help: Data about people: emails, phone numbers, IBANs, codice fiscale, partita IVA, card numbers.

IDENTITY.label: Identity
IDENTITY.help: This machine's identity: your user name in paths, the host name, your git name and email.

CUSTOM.label: Your terms and formats
CUSTOM.help: A term from your own list (client names, project code names, internal domains), or a value one of your recognizers found.

LLM.label: Local reviewer
LLM.help: Found by your local reviewer, a language model on your own server that reads what the detectors left in clear. Drawn with a dashed line: it is a judgement, not a pattern match.

NER.label: Model detection
NER.help: Found by the local language model: names, street addresses, cities. Drawn with a dashed line: it is a judgement, not a pattern match.

STRUCT.label: Data value
STRUCT.help: A value of a table, a JSON document or key=value pairs in a tool's output, masked by strict data mode or a field rule. It is masked in its structure only: the same word elsewhere is left alone.

UNKNOWN.label: Unknown
UNKNOWN.help: Latet lost track of this value's type.

blocked.label: Blocked
blocked.help: Latet stopped this request: it would have sent a sensitive value in clear. Nothing left your machine; the agent got an error.

leak.label: Leak
leak.help: The check found sensitive values in clear in this request. See the list on the request page (types only, never the values).

error.label: Error
error.help: The exchange failed: the provider answered with an error or the connection broke.

uninspected.label: Not inspected
uninspected.help: Part of this request was not read ({{detail}}): documents, images by their address, and images while text recognition is off or not installed. Latet 0.11 refuses such a request; an older Latet sent it as it was.

degraded.label: Degraded
degraded.help: A detector did not run fully ({{detail}}), so some values may have been missed.

unknown-route.label: Unknown route
unknown-route.help: Latet doesn't know this API route, so it forwarded the request without inspecting it.

project-off.label: Latet off
project-off.help: Latet is off in this project (your own settings for it). Latet 0.11 refuses such a request rather than sending it unmasked; an older Latet sent it as it was.

project-claimed.label: Project claimed
project-claimed.help: A header or a folder in the request's text named its project, which Latet cannot verify: only the project's rules that add protection applied, never its loosenings or its exceptions.

withheld.label: Withheld
withheld.help: The dump guard kept a tool output from the model: it held more personal values than allowed in one output. The model was told to ask for fewer rows, or for counts instead.

history.label: From the history
history.help: The values in clear were in this conversation's history, which Latet never masked: it began before Latet was on, or was resumed from then. Claude Code sends that history with every request, so start a new conversation (/clear).

image.label: Image
image.help: An image of this request was read on this computer ({{detail}}). Masked: the values read in it were covered with their fakes before it left. Withheld: it could not be read, so it was not sent.

verified.label: Verified
verified.help: The final check ran on what was about to leave and found nothing sensitive in clear.

auto-mode-review.label: Auto mode review
auto-mode-review.help: Claude Code's auto mode reviewer: a model asked whether an action is safe to run. It is sent your OS user name, your home and working directories and your git author.

outbound.label: Stand-in to a tool outside
outbound.help: A tool that runs outside your computer (a web search, a page, a claude.ai connector, a tool the provider runs) got, or would have got, a value Latet replaced: it works on the stand-in, not on the real value.

route-bypass.label: Around Latet
route-bypass.help: Claude Code was set to send its requests elsewhere, around Latet: its prompts were stopped. The reason says which settings file did it.

data.title: Production data
data.description: Query results, API answers and logs the agent reads: tables, JSON and key=value pairs. Columns and keys named like secrets (password, api_key, *_token) are always masked.

strict.title: Strict data mode
strict.help: Every value of a table, a JSON document or key=value pairs in a tool's output is masked; column and key names stay. The same value always gets the same fake, so counts, groups and joins still work, and a query written with a fake runs with the real value. Files the agent reads and web pages are left alone, unless a rule below names them.
strict.switch: Mask every value of tool outputs
strict.profileHelp: As the profile: on with Max, off with Balanced and Secrets only. Strict or Normal stays as you set it, whatever the profile.

files.title: Files that count as data
files.help: Path patterns, with * for any characters: *.json, exports/**, .env*. A pattern without a slash names a file by its name. When the agent reads such a file, every value in it is masked, found by the file's format: JSON, tables (CSV, TSV), .env and properties, YAML. A markdown file only when a pattern names markdown (*.md), and then only its tables. This holds whether strict data mode is on or off. A pattern as broad as *.json also covers package.json: name the folders that hold data (exports/**).
files.empty: No file: the files the agent reads are left alone.

hosts.title: Web addresses that count as data
hosts.help: Host names, with * for any characters: api.internal.example.com, *.salesforce.com. A pattern for every subdomain, such as *.salesforce.com, also covers the domain itself. A page a web tool (WebFetch) fetches from such an address is masked as a tool's output: every value of its tables, JSON and key=value pairs. This holds whether strict data mode is on or off.
hosts.empty: No address: web pages are left alone.

tools.title: Tools and MCP servers that count as data
tools.help: Tool names, with * for any characters: mcp__postgres__* (every tool of the MCP server postgres), Bash. With strict data mode on and this list empty, every tool's output counts, except the tools that read files and the web tools (WebSearch, WebFetch), whose results are public content; with names here, only those tools' outputs count.

fields.title: Field rules
fields.help: The values of a column or a JSON key (a path like items[].sku; * matches any characters), masked as a type of your own, or kept in clear in strict data mode. Secret columns stay masked all the same.

A project's settings, and its repository's latet.yaml, may only refuse (`unknown_members: refuse`).

refusal.auth: Credentials could not be read, or were refused.

refusal.parse: A part of it could not be read as its protocol says, so Latet could not account for all of it.

remedy.exception: An exact request exception lets it through: name the header or the parameter under request_exceptions in your settings, then approve the change on the Approvals page.

remedy.renew: Renewing it is a new approval: change the exception in your settings, then approve the change.
remedy.resource: List the value under request_resources in your settings for this destination.
remedy.again: Sent again, it goes under the settings now in force.
remedy.websocket: A WebSocket takes no request exception in this version of Latet.
remedy.strict: `unknown_members: refuse`, in your settings, in this project's or in your company's policy, refuses such members. With `unknown_members: check`, Latet reads such a member whole and sends it when nothing in it would be masked and it names no file, address, stored conversation or model.
